clone_manifest_note: One entry per clone of each sweep; instance ids are positional (clone-<role>-<arch>-<index>).
concordance_note: One value per dataset, scored against Ensembl VEP 116.3's archived output (perl_reference names the sets): every clone of both architectures of the concordance sweep reported the same raw and adjusted F1 and the same tuple counts (F1 is deterministic per binary and architecture-independent). The README's "Current release" tables render these values from this record at nine decimal places, recomputed from the tuple counts. Adjusted F1 is 1.0 on every dataset. Tuple counts move against v0.6.0 on 4 of 4 cells; the movement is in this record, previous_release_concordance beside concordance per cell and per file for the structural-variant cells. The paired run of the previous release (previous_release_concordance, the same day, the same clones' protocol, the same Ensembl VEP 116.3 reference) is the comparison basis: raw F1 is below it on the datasets raw_f1_fall names, by rows of the documented divergences alone, counted there by class (the whole-genome population datasets under whole_genome); adjusted F1 is 1.0 on every dataset with no row left.
dataset_inventory_sha256_note: One value per sweep, identical across its clones of both architectures (each clone entry carries its own). The concordance sweep's clones also synced the archived Perl ground truth the comparator reads, so its inventory covers more files than the wall-time sweep's.

field_agreement.note: compare_vep_fields.py on every concordance clone of the release (v1.0.0) and of the previous release (v0.6.0), the same protocol, both against the Ensembl VEP 116.3 reference set: per dataset the key totals and, per output column, the rows compared (both engines wrote the key), equal and differing. Only s01 and s02 are field-compared in this fleet: the structural-variant cells (s07 to s10) have no per-column comparator. columns_differing_from_previous lists every (dataset, column) whose compared/equal/differ counts differ from the previous release's paired clone; a listed column whose compared count rose with differ 0 means the released version agrees with Ensembl VEP on more tuples than the previous release did, and an empty list means it agrees column for column exactly where the previous release did.

absent.reason: reads no Ensembl VEP transcript cache

statements.says: its gene models come from a GFF3 file
it reads no Ensembl VEP transcript cache
statements.words: fastVEP never opens VEP's transcript cache or a database

harness_skip_fields_note: The per-column field comparator (compare_vep_fields.py) ran on every concordance clone of both releases; field_agreement summarises the released version's per-dataset, per-column agreement and names every column whose agreement differs from the previous release's.
linker_note: The minimum glibc the measured binaries need (glibc_floor), read from their ELF version needs by the build's floor check, and the linker that produced them (linker), both read from the build markers of both architectures; the floor and the linker are the release workflow's, so the measured binaries are linked as the release archives are.
methodology_note: c9gd.8xlarge (ARM Graviton5) and c8id.8xlarge (Intel x86_64), 32 vCPU / 64 GiB / local NVMe instance store, spec-matched, the newest available class per architecture (Graviton5 against 8th-generation Intel); 5 fresh clones per architecture booting the stock AL2023 base image, each syncing the dataset to local NVMe. The wall-time sweep runs scripts/concordance/run_clone_measurement.sh --walltime-only (--fork 16, sites-only inputs): one cold-cache warmup (discarded) and one timed measurement per cell, then self-terminates; median and P5/P95 across the clones per cell (Weibull, R type 6). The concordance sweep runs the same script without --walltime-only, so each clone also computes the 6-cell concordance report against the archived Perl ground truth, on r9gd.8xlarge and r8id.8xlarge (32 vCPU / 256 GiB); its wall times are not used, because the comparator running between datasets perturbs the timed run that follows a warmup on the largest output.
per_cell_aggregates_note: Wall time per (arch, dataset) over the completed clones of the wall-time sweep (median and quantiles by the Weibull estimator, R type 6); each of those clones' entry under clones carries the per-dataset wall time it reported (wall_time_sec), so every aggregate re-derives from this record. The README's "Current release" table renders these values.

population_concordance.note: Whole-genome concordance of the released binary against Ensembl VEP 116.3's archived output on four population datasets, one clone per chromosome shard (the pool arch's), the same comparator, cache and reference FASTA as the genome-wide ClinVar and structural-variant cells. A variant is one VCF record; a tuple is one output row reduced to (Location, Allele, Feature, Feature_type, Consequence set); F1 is pooled by summed counts (micro-F1), raw with nothing set aside and adjusted with the documented divergence classes set aside. Wall time per shard is kept with the run's outputs as information only.

not_applied.reason: the reference set holds no seeded run for the cell, so the class was not applied: the count is the values that differ under it, an upper bound, and none of them is a residual row

public_build_inputs_note: Git object ids of the build inputs at source_commit (crates tree, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .cargo/config.toml), re-derived by the build host from the extracted source and recorded with the binary; a tag whose inputs equal these carries the code that was measured. src_tree_ids are the git tree ids of each crate's source directory at source_commit; a release tag whose crates/<name>/src trees equal them and whose Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and .cargo/config.toml blobs equal the ids above carries the code that was measured, whatever its crates tree id: a test or documentation file under crates/ that changes after the measurement does not enter the binary.

raw_f1_fall.note: Every cell is counted in pairs, one tuple of each engine a pair, newly set aside in this version. On ClinVar GRCh37 the pairs equal the fall of the raw intersection, 586. On ClinVar GRCh38 2,428 pairs are counted and the raw intersection falls by 2,427: 1 tuple that v0.6.0 left outside the intersection is inside it in this version. On the structural-variant sets of GRCh38 the 2,060 pairs are counted once across the 16 files, the fall of the union's intersection (1,427,654 to 1,425,594), and the intersection summed over the files falls by 2,067. The whole-genome datasets are counted in pairs under the classes that grew, one tuple of each engine a pair: each lists the classes that set aside more tuples in this version than in v0.6.0's re-scoring, each at the count it grew by, and its shortfall is their sum. Against that re-scoring, on gnomad_v4.1_genomes the raw intersection falls by 128 and 133 pairs are counted (`stop_codon_removed_without_stop_codon_test` holds 2 fewer, `stop_retained_without_stop_codon_test` holds 2 fewer, `start_cooccurrence_swap` holds 1 fewer); on gnomad_v2.1.1_genomes the raw intersection falls by 120 and 200 pairs are counted (`stop_codon_removed_without_stop_codon_test` holds 72 fewer, `stop_retained_without_stop_codon_test` holds 7 fewer, `start_cooccurrence_swap` holds 1 fewer); on 1000g_phase3_20130502 the raw intersection falls by 750 and 750 pairs are counted (no class holds fewer tuples); on 1000g_highcov_20220422 the raw intersection falls by 257 and 258 pairs are counted (`start_cooccurrence_swap` holds 1 fewer); on all datasets the raw intersection falls by 1,255 and 1,341 pairs are counted (`stop_codon_removed_without_stop_codon_test` holds 74 fewer, `stop_retained_without_stop_codon_test` holds 9 fewer, `start_cooccurrence_swap` holds 3 fewer). Where a tuple that left an older class went, to a newer class or back inside the intersection, was not read on these datasets. The chromosome 20 shard of 1000 Genomes Phase 3 was scored with the comparison rule of the commit that adds this record, which takes under the documented difference `splice_term_past_the_record_span` one row of an insertion written after one kept reference base at an intron of one base; no other shard was scored again.

rustc_note: The compiler of the measured binaries, read from the build markers of both architectures; it is the toolchain the release workflow pins, so the release assets are builds of the same source, lockfile and compiler, identified by their own digests in SHA256SUMS.

same_day_control.note: Both binaries under the release protocol on the same day (--walltime-only, the discarded warmup's output flushed and deleted before the timed run), on the same instance types and images: the released version (5 + 5 clones) and the previous release (3 + 3 clones) agree within 8.0% in median wall time on 8 of 8 cells and within 4.6% in median user CPU time on every cell above 60 CPU-seconds.

scope: vep-rs alone: the released version's concordance on the cells s01, s02, s07, s08, s09, s10 against Ensembl VEP 116.3's archived output (perl_reference names the sets) and its own wall times on both architectures, stated in the README beside the paper's figures, which do not change. Perl VEP and fastVEP are not re-measured here, and no ratio against the paper's medians is stated: the release protocol deletes the discarded warmup's output before the timed run and the paper's did not. The same-day control below is the comparison the README cites.
sites_only_note: Every timed input is sites-only; s09 and s10 are pointer datasets into the per-file structural-variant results of s07 and s08.
warmup_output_discarded_note: Before each timed run the harness flushes and deletes the discarded warmup's output (scripts/concordance/run_clone_measurement.sh, discard_warmup_output), so the timed run starts with the memory the warmup had.
